questions.q: What table stores role records in ServiceNow?
options: sys_user_has_role
sys_user_group
sys_user_role
sys_user_grmember
questions.explain: sys_user_role is the table of role records; sys_user_has_role is the separate join table tracking which users hold which roles.

questions.q: What is the fundamental difference between what a group controls versus what a role controls?
options: There is no real difference; they are interchangeable
A group controls who's on a team for routing and visibility; a role controls what a user is permitted to do
A role controls team routing, and a group controls permissions
Groups only apply to end users, roles only apply to agents
questions.explain: A user can be a group member with zero roles and have almost no functional permissions — group membership and permission are separate systems.

questions.q: What does the 'Contains Roles' related list on a role record actually do?
options: It's purely cosmetic documentation with no functional effect
It lists which users are assigned that role
It defines other roles that are implicitly, automatically granted to anyone holding this role
It restricts the role from being assigned to more than one user
questions.explain: This is real inheritance — ACLs checking for a contained role will pass for a user who only has the containing role, via the platform's effective-roles resolution.

questions.q: Why does granting someone the admin role carry outsized risk compared to most other roles?
options: admin has no practical effect by itself
admin contains nearly every other role in the system, so granting it implicitly grants the functional equivalent of dozens of roles at once
admin only affects the Service Catalog
admin must always be paired with itil_admin to work
questions.explain: Because admin sits at the top of the role containment chain, assigning it is never really 'just one role' — it's everything admin contains too.

questions.q: Before casually granting a user a role you haven't used before, what should you check first, and why?
options: Nothing — role names are self-explanatory and never contain other roles
Only whether the user is active
The role's Contains Roles related list, since a narrow-sounding role might implicitly grant far more access than intended
Whether the role has a Group Email configured
questions.explain: Checking containment before granting is the practical face of least privilege — a role can grant much more than its name suggests.
